text: Fixed. `gin.Error` declared `func (msg *Error) Unwrap() error`, so only `*Error` satisfied the `Unwrap() error` interface used by `errors.Is`/`errors.As`. A plain `Error` value therefore had no unwrap method and the chain stopped there, silently reporting "not found". I changed the receiver to a value receiver (`func (msg Error) Unwrap() error`) in errors.go, so both `Error` and `*Error` participate in the unwrap chain; the pointer form keeps working since a pointer's method set includes value methods. Verified with a scratch test covering `errors.Is`, `errors.As`, `errors.Unwrap` for both the value and pointer forms, and the full existing test suite (`go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`) still passes.

Fixed. In `responseWriter.WriteHeader` (response_writer.go), when the response was already written the code printed a warning but still assigned `w.status = code`, so `Status()` reported a code that was never sent to the client. I added an early `return` in that branch so the recorded status stays the one that was actually written (the warning is still printed). Verified with a scratch test reproducing your sequence (200 + WriteHeaderNow, then WriteHeader(401) -> Status() stays 200) and the full suite still passes.

Looking into it: routes registered after the first request leave pooled contexts with params slices too small for the newly added route, so parameters get dropped (and a wildcard route can even panic). Fixing in progress.
Looking into it: the case-insensitive path lookup assumes the first child is the wildcard one, so a static sibling under the same prefix leads to the "invalid node type" panic. Fixing in progress.
Looking into it: NegotiateFormat indexes the offer string with the accepted string's length, so a longer Accept value panics. Fixing in progress.
Looking into it: FileAttachment writes the filename into the Content-Disposition header without escaping quotes/backslashes. Fixing in progress.

Fixed. Contexts are pooled and their `params`/`skippedNodes` slices were sized from `engine.maxParams`/`maxSections` at allocation time, so a context allocated before your route existed kept a zero-capacity slice; `getValue` then silently skipped saving params (and panicked on a catch-all). `handleHTTPRequest` now grows those slices when the currently registered routes need more room, so routes registered at runtime behave exactly like routes registered up front. Verified with your exact scenario (404 first, then 200 with name=john, last_name=smith, wild=/is/super/great) and the full suite passes.

Fixed. In `findCaseInsensitivePathRec` the wildcard child was assumed to be `n.children[0]`, but the tree keeps the wildcard child last, so with a static sibling the switch fell through to `panic("invalid node type")`. The lookup now tries the static children first (same case-insensitive rune matching as elsewhere) and only falls back to the last child, the wildcard one. `/PREFIX/XXX` now 301-redirects to `/prefix/xxx` and `/prefix/a/b/c` returns 404. Full suite passes.

Fixed. `NegotiateFormat` looped over the accepted string while indexing the offer string with the same index, so an Accept value longer than the offer read past the end. The loop now stops at the shorter of the two, so `image/tiff-fx` vs `image/tiff` returns "" instead of panicking; wildcard and prefix matching behavior is unchanged. Full suite passes.

Fixed. `FileAttachment` interpolated the filename into the quoted-string of `Content-Disposition` verbatim. It now escapes `"` and `\` (RFC 7230 quoted-pair) via a new `escapeQuotes` helper in utils.go, so `evil"; dummy="x.sh` becomes `attachment; filename="evil\"; dummy=\"x.sh"` — one well-formed filename, no injected parameters. Plain names and the UTF-8 branch are unchanged. Full suite passes.
